75	  where ABAB genuinely mimics an ABCA singleton within the scale prior —
76	  and the near-CNP *hole* pair is close and balanced (beat-like on short
77	  1/B records). Both wash out by |n| ≳ 2–3×10¹².
78	- **ABCB**: a pair partitioning F_L with a *light Dirac* partner — a
79	  shape-discriminated variant of the two-tone case (citation-grade).
80	- **Mixed stacking domains**: templates superposed, each grouping checked
81	  against the **same** F_L (domains share the gated density). Peak
82	  *amplitudes* track the domains' geometric weighting.
83	- **A tone at F_L is not automatically ABCA**: an ABAB pair sums to F_L, so a
84	  **magnetic breakdown** orbit through both pockets or an intermodulation tone
85	  lands exactly at F_L and mimics the ABCA singleton — and unlike the trilayer
86	  case, ABAB inter-block breakdown is **symmetry-allowed** (no parity
87	  protection between the two bilayer-like blocks), so treat the sum-tone
88	  confound as *expected*, not exotic. A set {f₁, f₂, ≈F_L} underdetermines
89	  mixed domains; discriminate before claiming one (Verify: F_L-tone origin —
90	  mandatory for any singleton call where partner tones are resolved).
91	
92	Against the trilayer read, this one is structurally **easier at design
93	densities |n| ≳ 2–3×10¹²**: the dominant tones themselves separate (ABAB's
94	biggest tone at ≈ 0.72–0.79·F_L vs ABCA's at F_L), and the ABAB partner tone
95	carries ~21–28% of F_L rather than a few percent. The discriminating
96	evidence is the dominant-tone *position* plus the partition — not a
97	small-tone hunt. The advantage evaporates in the low-|n| exception regimes
98	above — design around them (Step 2).
99	
100	Four disciplines keep it honest (unchanged from the trilayer method; stated
101	here because this recipe runs standalone):
102	
103	- **Pin the scale before you reject.** The lever arm is one global number the
104	  Luttinger relations pin — a singleton sits at F_L, a pair sums to F_L. Fit
105	  that single in-band scale to the *whole* peak set first; a peak is "above
106	  F_L" only after the scale is pinned. Multiple populations (mixed domains)
107	  over-determine the scale — leverage, not noise. Any later scale change is
108	  retroactive — re-read the whole set.
109	- **Classify on frequencies, never amplitudes.** Amplitudes fold in field,
110	  Dingle damping, and domain weighting; frequencies carry the pocket areas.
111	- **Screen harmonics first — and Luttinger-aware.** Drop any peak at an
112	  integer multiple of a stronger fundamental (confirm by n-dependence — a
113	  harmonic tracks k·f exactly; a real pocket follows its own Onsager curve),
114	  but never discard a tone as a harmonic when doing so breaks the partition
115	  sum: the ABAB pair's ratio ≈ 2.6 drifts through 3× with density, and a
116	  ratio-only screen eats the real heavy tone exactly there [our-model,
117	  synthetic replay]. The n-dependence screen plus the sum decide, not the
118	  ratio alone.
119	- **Read each Rxx channel separately, never averaged.** Each pair probes a
120	  region of a possibly-mosaic flake; the call is **per region**, and "most
121	  channels uninformative" is a normal outcome.
122	
123	Two design facts:
124	
125	- **D ≈ 0 is the operating point.** Finite D gaps ABCA, reshapes ABAB's
126	  overlap and hybridizes its blocks, and splits ABAB valleys. A quantitative
127	  small-residual-D robustness statement is pending the model — treat residual
128	  D as "keep it small," a heuristic, not a guarantee (survey §3).
129	- **No side prior.** Both signs get a spot check (Step 3); the fan follows the
130	  cleaner side.
131	
132	## Recipe
133	
134	**Step 0 — mine what's already on disk.** An existing D = 0 fan with adequate
135	low-field reach already answers most of this via per-column FFT (Step 4);
136	existing 0 T gate maps answer Step 1.
137	
138	**Step 1 — B = 0 (n, D) gate map + the (n, D) conversion.** As in the trilayer
139	sibling, verbatim: calibration from `device-init/cnp-and-dline-calibration.md`
140	(ratio data-calibrated, scale geometry-prior); identify clean hole- and
141	electron-side regions and the D = 0 line; flag arms going insulating; pick
142	voltage pairs metallic across the planned n-range. One tetralayer addendum: an
143	insulating CNP at D ≈ 0 is **not** a stacking read — it has three candidate
144	parents (ABCB intrinsic gap; ABCA under residual D; interaction-gapped ABAB in
145	ultraclean devices) — record it and move on (survey §5).
146	
147	**Step 2 — feasibility (binding: compute, don't eyeball).** The reference
148	frequency is **F_L = (h/4e)·n**. From it and the template partitions, compute
149	the three design numbers before any sweep:
150	
151	- **Δ(1/B) resolution** — Nyquist on F_L (the fastest expected tone):
152	  Δ(1/B) ≤ 1/(2·F_L).
153	- **Tone separation** — the binding resolution case is separating the ABAB
154	  heavy tone from an ABCA singleton (F_L), and resolving the ABAB partner
155	  with ≥ ~5 periods: (1/B_lo − 1/B_hi) ≥ 5/f_partner. Take both tones'
156	  frequencies from the **model's F(n) table**
157	  (`hera/models/tetralayer_fs_count/`), not the bare 0.72/0.28 ratios — and
158	  pick design densities |n| ≳ 2–3×10¹² where the templates separate: at
159	  +1×10¹² the ABAB heavy tone sits within ~5% of F_L and the partner at
160	  ~0.6 T is unresolvable in any practical window [our-model].
161	- **The field window** — onset is measured in Step 3, not computed; keep the
162	  ~100 mT-scale heuristic as an expectation only.
163	
164	**Step 3 — SdH spot checks (`sdh-spot-check.md`).** Two spot checks — large
165	hole and large electron density (push |n| high within gate limits and any
166	contact-stress ceiling) — each fixed-(n, D = 0), uniform in 1/B, Δ(1/B) from
167	Step 2. From each FFT: which tones are present, and which side is cleaner. A
168	clean spot check can be **decisive on its own**; lock its sampling, settling,
169	and sensitivity and hand them, with the measured onset, to Step 4.
170	
171	**Step 4 — full Landau fan + per-column FFT (`landau-fan.md`).** Fan on the
172	cleaner side over a decently large density window at D = 0. Field range from
173	Step 3 (onset → B_lo; period-count extrapolation to the low-density edge sets
174	B_hi — the ABAB partner tone at the lowest fan density is the binding case).
175	Inherit the spot check's Δ(1/B) and settling. FFT each n-column; read peak set
176	vs F_L, the Luttinger partition, and each tone's n-dependence in one object.
177	
178	**Step 5 — F(n) across density (the refinement).** (1) **Partition
179	robustness** — f₁(n) + f₂(n) = F_L(n) across density is algebraic (no model);
180	a coincidental one-density match will not hold. (2) **Branch labeling** —
181	overlay measured F(n) on the model curves (Verify: forward-model comparison):
182	ABAB branches are *both parabolic* and are labeled by the frequency ratio and
183	per-branch mass (Verify: LK), **not** by shape; a light *Dirac-shaped* branch
184	(supra-linear F(n) at low n against the model) points at ABCB's J = 1 partner
185	[citation-grade — report as candidate, hedge accordingly]. The binary
186	ABAB-pair vs ABCA-singleton call needs only (1) plus the F_L-tone origin
187	discrimination.
188	
189	**Step 6 — high field (weak complement only).** There is **no tetralayer
190	Streda/Chern offset discriminator**: every 4L stacking carries 16 zero-energy
191	LLs — a ν = ±8, 12, 16 low-field ladder confirms the *layer number*, not the
192	stacking (survey §4; the layer-number check is itself useful — Verify:
193	adjacent-N). Stacking-dependent LL *fine structure* (two interleaved bilayer
194	ladders with mod-3 anticrossings vs a single bunched ladder) is qualitative —
195	no validated 4L LL model — so weight anything from it ≤ weak.
196	
197	**Step 7 — the call.** Output contract (all five parts mandatory):
198	
199	1. Per-region verdict on the STYLE strength scale: `channel/pair X: ABAB
200	   (strong) | ABCA (weak) | ABCB-candidate (consistent-with) | mixed-domain
201	   (consistent-with) | uninformative` — every verdict carries its weight word;
202	   bare leans are not verdicts.
203	2. Evidence list: each tone claimed, with frequency, (n, D) coordinates and
204	   density side, the Onsager-overlay artifact, and the Luttinger check.
205	3. Confidence + specific hedges (resolution limits, side/density, features
206	   searched-and-absent vs not-resolvable, domain/mosaic caveat, **absolute
207	   layer number** — if the peak set matches neither 4L template, the
208	   adjacent-N hypothesis belongs here before exotic explanations).
209	4. What would firm the call (other side, LK mass split, degeneracy audit,
210	   independent N-ID, a different rig/temperature).
211	5. **A "cannot tell" with reasons is a successful outcome. A confident call
212	   without feature-level evidence is a protocol violation.**
213	
214	## Verify
215	
216	- **TSV-first is mandatory for any classification-grade read.** Re-form
217	  Rxx(n, B) at native grid resolution (channel arithmetic per the device card)
218	  before any frequency claim; rendered monitor PNGs alias the SdH structure.
219	- **Onsager forward-model overlay.** Tool: `hera/models/tetralayer_fs_count/`
220	  (B = 0 FS count + Onsager F(n) + m*(n); ABAB SWMcC + ABCA 8-band continuum —
221	  semi-quantitative; validity stance in the model README). Overlay measured
222	  per-column F(n) allowing a **single global density rescale** (~0.8–1.2
223	  plausible [heuristic — lever-arm prior]; far outside that band is a red
224	  flag, not a fit) — fit that one scale to the **whole** peak set before
225	  reading any tone against a template; a lone tone forced onto a template by
226	  a private rescale while a resolved partner closes the Luttinger sum at
227	  scale 1 is a mis-read, not a fit. **A pair summing to F_L is necessary,
228	  not sufficient, for ABAB.** For any two-tone pair, compute **both**
229	  overlays — the ABAB curves *and* the trilayer ML+BL curves
230	  (`hera/models/trilayer_fs_count/`) — and report which family the branches
231	  track across density; **do not absorb a partition mismatch as model error**
232	  (the partition is a trusted model output — README validity stance): a pair
233	  tracking the trilayer curves is an adjacent-N read (Adjacent-N check
234	  below), not off-model ABAB [our-measurement, harness replay 2026-07-20 —
235	  agents mapped a trilayer 0.15/0.85 pair into 4L templates]. Partition
236	  magnitude alone cannot decide — the ABAB partner fraction sweeps
237	  ~0.06–0.44 with density and crosses the trilayer ~0.11–0.15 near
238	  |n| ≈ 2×10¹² [our-model]; the discriminator is the trajectory, not a
239	  ratio. Two branches on the ABAB curves *and* the F_L-tone origin passed is
240	  **strong** ABAB; a single branch on the ABCA curve with the origin
241	  discrimination passed is **strong** ABCA. Confound: mixed domains
242	  superpose templates on one F_L — resolve by the combinatorics, harmonic
243	  screen, and per-channel reads (Why).
244	- **F_L-tone origin (breakdown | ABCA domain | mixing) — mandatory before any
245	  singleton call where partner tones are resolved** (ABAB breakdown is
246	  symmetry-allowed, Why): (1) **B-window split** — FFT low-B and high-B halves
247	  separately; a breakdown/mixing tone strengthens with B relative to the
248	  fundamentals, a real pocket keeps its own Dingle envelope — but a *null*
249	  split in a narrow field window is weak: breakdown with onset scale above
250	  the window top is unresolvable there (absence claims cite resolvability)
251	  [our-model, synthetic replay]; (2) **grid-change
252	  reproduction** (`sdh-spot-check.md` Verify) retires sampling-alias origins;
253	  (3) the per-branch **LK mass** (below) is decisive. An unresolved remainder
254	  is a fork to report (STYLE rule 14).
255	- **LK mass split + beat exclusion** *(our-model expectation)*: the ABAB
256	  branches' masses differ by ≈ φ² ≈ 2.6× — per-branch LK masses
257	  (`temperature-dependence` Flavor B) cleanly separate two genuine bands from
258	  one band plus artifact; compare against the model's m*(n), never a
259	  light/heavy prior alone. Beat exclusion as in the trilayer sibling: a
260	  coexisting component **lighter** than the main branch cannot be a beat
261	  (decisive); at-or-above decides nothing alone.
262	- **Degeneracy audit.** F_L = (h/4e)·n assumes the symmetric 4-fold metal —
263	  expected at D ≈ 0, |n| ~ 10¹², kelvin-scale temperatures (survey §6), but
264	  verify in-data: after the scale is pinned on the full set, a peak set
265	  sitting at 2× or 4× its g = 4-predicted positions reads as flavor
266	  polarization (g = 2 / g = 1) and **suspends the g = 4 combinatorics** —
267	  escalate with the survey §6 reference rather than reading tones as
268	  supra-F_L pockets.
269	- **Adjacent-N check.** If the peak set matches neither 4L template **as a
270	  model overlay** — including a pair that sums to F_L but tracks the trilayer
271	  ML+BL curves rather than the ABAB curves (dual overlay above; a lopsided
272	  pair still passes the loose "pair partitioning F_L" template) — run the
273	  trilayer templates (ML+BL pair with a *small* partner; ABC singleton) and
274	  the pentalayer expectation (2+2+1) before anything exotic — optical-contrast
275	  N-assignment can misassign absolute layer number while resolving steps well
276	  (survey §7). Confound [our-model, synthetic replay]: a heavily damped
277	  singleton (large-m\* regions — e.g. the ABCA flat-band edge) plus a noise
278	  peak mimics the small-partner trilayer template on *single columns* — the
279	  adjacent-N call is a **cross-column consensus read**: the claimed partner
280	  must track its own Onsager curve across density and clear the local noise
281	  floor, never a one-column fit. A ν = 8, 12, 16 QH ladder (Step 6) or
282	  magneto-Raman G-band anticrossings (`hera/docs/papers/1501.06764/paper.md`)
283	  are independent N checks; state which N the transport actually supports in
284	  the hedges.
285	- **FFT stability sweep.** Vary detrender and window; a real peak sharpens as
286	  the 1/B record lengthens, an artifact wanders. Detrend on even-in-B data
287	  **before** interpolating to 1/B (detrending after manufactures
288	  low-frequency artifacts — paper-data, `hera/docs/papers/2606.05356/paper.md`
289	  resolution ladder). A frequency whose value or n-slope flips across
290	  reasonable extraction choices is a **fork to report, not refine** (STYLE
291	  rule 14).
292	- **Acquisition quality is empirical — compare at a shared density.** As in
293	  the trilayer sibling, verbatim: quality is a property of how a column was
294	  acquired; a lower-quality measurement never overturns a higher-quality one;
295	  the stopping rule (finer B resolves no new tones ⇒ count complete at this
296	  T/mobility) holds only on adequately acquired data. Resolution-ladder
297	  anchor: SdH from ≈ 0.1 T needs μ ≳ 10⁵ cm²/Vs (paper-data, Grushina — a
298	  suspended-device benchmark; expect a higher onset at lower quantum
299	  mobility, and read onset empirically in Step 3).
300	- **Luttinger sum.** Σf = n (g = 4) across the fan is the model-independent
301	  consistency check and the constraint that pins the global scale. A peak set
302	  that **cannot** satisfy the sum after the harmonic screen and stability
303	  sweep is a reportable state, not an extraction failure — R4G hosts
304	  documented non-Onsager regimes, though concentrated at large |D| / low n
305	  (survey §6); at the D ≈ 0 operating point treat it first as a degeneracy or
306	  N-assignment problem (audits above).
307	- **CNP magnitude is not a stacking read.** Insulating-CNP behavior has three
308	  candidate parents at N = 4 (survey §5) on top of the domain-shunting
309	  confound — feed it into the per-channel picture as consistent-with at
310	  most, never a standalone call.
311	- **Lever-arm / Nyquist at design time.** As in the trilayer sibling: ray
312	  slopes / frequencies must quantize against the (n, D) calibration; the
313	  B-axis SdH period sets the fan's B-row spacing — a fan failing the
314	  `landau-fan.md` Nyquist check in the claim window is uninformative there,
315	  re-measure.
316	
317	## Examples
318	
319	*(No live tetralayer sessions yet — this section seeds from the first
320	campaign/replay burns. Channel facts stay in device cards and notebook
321	indexes, never here — STYLE rule 11.)*
322	
323	## Next
324	
325	- **ABAB-confirmed** (pair partitioning F_L, Onsager-tracking, φ²-split LK
326	  masses): conventional tetralayer — campaign value is QH degeneracy-lifting /
327	  even-N interaction physics (ultraclean devices only); otherwise deprioritise.
328	- **ABCA-leaning** (singleton at F_L with the origin discrimination passed):
329	  the interesting outcome — flat-band / correlated / superconducting candidate
330	  at high D and mK temperatures (`hera/docs/papers/2606.05356/paper.md` for
331	  the phase-diagram map). Verify with D-gap systematics (per-channel,
332	  domain-aware) and plan the low-T campaign the physics deserves.
333	- **ABCB-candidate** (light Dirac partner + intrinsic-gap constellation):
334	  rare and citation-grade — what would firm it: Raman G-peak position and
335	  near-field imaging on the region, plus a model upgrade before any strong
336	  transport claim.
337	- **Mixed-domain device**: map which pairs probe which stacking; decide
338	  whether any single-domain region supports the science goal before more
339	  magnet time.
340	- **Resolution-limited cannot-tell**: state the onset-field / mobility number
341	  and what side, density, or temperature would change it — a device-quality /
342	  rig choice, not more sweeps on this rig.
343

# Tetralayer stacking identification by Fermi-surface counting (ABAB / ABCA / ABCB)

*Investigation — a decision procedure one level up from the measurement recipes
it orchestrates (`measurements/gatemap.md`, `measurements/sdh-spot-check.md`,
`measurements/landau-fan.md`), spanning multiple measurements rather than a single
sweep. Use the rig-appropriate variants; rig and device mechanics — magnet
discipline, gate wiring, validators — live in the device card and session brief,
not here. Trilayer devices use the sibling `trilayer-stacking-fs-count.md`; the
device card's material line routes.*

**Reference**: `hera/docs/tetralayer-stacking-extraction-survey.md` — the survey
that grounds this recipe, synthesising Min–MacDonald 2008
(`hera/docs/papers/0711.4333/paper.md`), Koshino–McCann 2011
(`hera/docs/papers/1104.0794/paper.md`), Grushina et al. 2015
(`hera/docs/papers/1501.06764/paper.md`), and Kalantre et al. 2026
(`hera/docs/papers/2606.05356/paper.md`). Read it first; every band-structure
claim below is grounded there.

## What

Classify the stacking order of a tetralayer-graphene device — ABAB (Bernal),
ABCA (rhombohedral), or ABCB (mixed) — by **counting distinct Fermi surfaces**
from Shubnikov–de Haas frequency content at controlled D ≈ 0, read as a peak
set against the Luttinger frequency. Output is a **region-resolved,
evidence-cited, hedged call**, not a headline.

## When

- A **dual-gated** tetralayer device of unknown or unverified stacking is loaded
  and gated, where you can sit at D = 0 and sweep n independently. (No
  single-gated tetralayer procedure exists in the corpus — a single-gated 4L
  device is an uncovered case to flag, not to improvise.)
- Stacking determines everything downstream (ABCA hosts the flat-band /
  correlated / superconducting physics; ABAB is conventional; ABCB is a
  metastable gapped oddity), so this is typically among the *first science
  questions* of a tetralayer campaign.
- Also worth running when stacking was assigned optically / by Raman only —
  transport is the in-situ check, and exfoliated multilayer flakes commonly
  host **mixed stacking domains**, so different contact pairs can disagree.
  (Raman side: `raman-stacking-id.md`; reconciling: `stacking-raman-transport-fusion.md`.)

Prerequisites: gates calibrated with validators committed (device-init
recipes), and at least one four-terminal Rxx channel with credible contacts and
quantum mobility high enough to reach SdH onset in the planned field window
(Step 3 decides this). Step 1 handles CNP identification and the (n, D)
conversion — a CNP that cannot be positively identified is itself an outcome to
surface, not a precondition.

## Why

The three stackings differ in Fermi-surface count *and* in where their tones
sit (`hera/docs/tetralayer-stacking-extraction-survey.md` §1–2):

- **ABAB**: two bilayer-like parabolic bands (effective interlayer couplings
  1.618γ₁ / 0.618γ₁) coexist → **2 Fermi surfaces**, densities partitioning
  ∝ mass.
- **ABCA**: a single chiral J = 4 quartic band with trigonal-warping Lifshitz
  structure confined to low density → **1 Fermi surface** at the ~10¹²
  operating density.
- **ABCB**: a cubic band plus a Dirac-like band over an intrinsic ~9 meV CNP
  gap → **2 Fermi surfaces** with a light, velocity-renormalized Dirac partner
  (citation-grade — no validated model backs quantitative ABCB reads).

**The read is the peak set against the Luttinger frequency.** F_L = (h/4e)·n
(g = 4, spin × valley, unbroken at the operating point — Verify: degeneracy
audit) is the predicted line, inheriting the lever-arm **scale** uncertainty
(geometry prior ~10–15% — `device-init/cnp-and-dline-calibration.md`), so F_L
is a **band, not a ceiling**. The templates:

- **ABCA**: one tone **at** F_L (the single pocket carries the full density).
- **ABAB**: a **pair** partitioning F_L at ≈ **0.72 / 0.28** (the φ² mass
  ratio; decomposition-limit values — the model's F(n) table is the design
  authority). Two exception regimes [our-model]: at low *electron* density
  the light pocket nearly empties and the heavy tone rides at ≈ 0.95·F_L —
  where ABAB genuinely mimics an ABCA singleton within the scale prior —
  and the near-CNP *hole* pair is close and balanced (beat-like on short
  1/B records). Both wash out by |n| ≳ 2–3×10¹².
- **ABCB**: a pair partitioning F_L with a *light Dirac* partner — a
  shape-discriminated variant of the two-tone case (citation-grade).
- **Mixed stacking domains**: templates superposed, each grouping checked
  against the **same** F_L (domains share the gated density). Peak
  *amplitudes* track the domains' geometric weighting.
- **A tone at F_L is not automatically ABCA**: an ABAB pair sums to F_L, so a
  **magnetic breakdown** orbit through both pockets or an intermodulation tone
  lands exactly at F_L and mimics the ABCA singleton — and unlike the trilayer
  case, ABAB inter-block breakdown is **symmetry-allowed** (no parity
  protection between the two bilayer-like blocks), so treat the sum-tone
  confound as *expected*, not exotic. A set {f₁, f₂, ≈F_L} underdetermines
  mixed domains; discriminate before claiming one (Verify: F_L-tone origin —
  mandatory for any singleton call where partner tones are resolved).

Against the trilayer read, this one is structurally **easier at design
densities |n| ≳ 2–3×10¹²**: the dominant tones themselves separate (ABAB's
biggest tone at ≈ 0.72–0.79·F_L vs ABCA's at F_L), and the ABAB partner tone
carries ~21–28% of F_L rather than a few percent. The discriminating
evidence is the dominant-tone *position* plus the partition — not a
small-tone hunt. The advantage evaporates in the low-|n| exception regimes
above — design around them (Step 2).

Four disciplines keep it honest (unchanged from the trilayer method; stated
here because this recipe runs standalone):

- **Pin the scale before you reject.** The lever arm is one global number the
  Luttinger relations pin — a singleton sits at F_L, a pair sums to F_L. Fit
  that single in-band scale to the *whole* peak set first; a peak is "above
  F_L" only after the scale is pinned. Multiple populations (mixed domains)
  over-determine the scale — leverage, not noise. Any later scale change is
  retroactive — re-read the whole set.
- **Classify on frequencies, never amplitudes.** Amplitudes fold in field,
  Dingle damping, and domain weighting; frequencies carry the pocket areas.
- **Screen harmonics first — and Luttinger-aware.** Drop any peak at an
  integer multiple of a stronger fundamental (confirm by n-dependence — a
  harmonic tracks k·f exactly; a real pocket follows its own Onsager curve),
  but never discard a tone as a harmonic when doing so breaks the partition
  sum: the ABAB pair's ratio ≈ 2.6 drifts through 3× with density, and a
  ratio-only screen eats the real heavy tone exactly there [our-model,
  synthetic replay]. The n-dependence screen plus the sum decide, not the
  ratio alone.
- **Read each Rxx channel separately, never averaged.** Each pair probes a
  region of a possibly-mosaic flake; the call is **per region**, and "most
  channels uninformative" is a normal outcome.

Two design facts:

- **D ≈ 0 is the operating point.** Finite D gaps ABCA, reshapes ABAB's
  overlap and hybridizes its blocks, and splits ABAB valleys. A quantitative
  small-residual-D robustness statement is pending the model — treat residual
  D as "keep it small," a heuristic, not a guarantee (survey §3).
- **No side prior.** Both signs get a spot check (Step 3); the fan follows the
  cleaner side.

## Recipe

**Step 0 — mine what's already on disk.** An existing D = 0 fan with adequate
low-field reach already answers most of this via per-column FFT (Step 4);
existing 0 T gate maps answer Step 1.

**Step 1 — B = 0 (n, D) gate map + the (n, D) conversion.** As in the trilayer
sibling, verbatim: calibration from `device-init/cnp-and-dline-calibration.md`
(ratio data-calibrated, scale geometry-prior); identify clean hole- and
electron-side regions and the D = 0 line; flag arms going insulating; pick
voltage pairs metallic across the planned n-range. One tetralayer addendum: an
insulating CNP at D ≈ 0 is **not** a stacking read — it has three candidate
parents (ABCB intrinsic gap; ABCA under residual D; interaction-gapped ABAB in
ultraclean devices) — record it and move on (survey §5).

**Step 2 — feasibility (binding: compute, don't eyeball).** The reference
frequency is **F_L = (h/4e)·n**. From it and the template partitions, compute
the three design numbers before any sweep:

- **Δ(1/B) resolution** — Nyquist on F_L (the fastest expected tone):
  Δ(1/B) ≤ 1/(2·F_L).
- **Tone separation** — the binding resolution case is separating the ABAB
  heavy tone from an ABCA singleton (F_L), and resolving the ABAB partner
  with ≥ ~5 periods: (1/B_lo − 1/B_hi) ≥ 5/f_partner. Take both tones'
  frequencies from the **model's F(n) table**
  (`hera/models/tetralayer_fs_count/`), not the bare 0.72/0.28 ratios — and
  pick design densities |n| ≳ 2–3×10¹² where the templates separate: at
  +1×10¹² the ABAB heavy tone sits within ~5% of F_L and the partner at
  ~0.6 T is unresolvable in any practical window [our-model].
- **The field window** — onset is measured in Step 3, not computed; keep the
  ~100 mT-scale heuristic as an expectation only.

**Step 3 — SdH spot checks (`sdh-spot-check.md`).** Two spot checks — large
hole and large electron density (push |n| high within gate limits and any
contact-stress ceiling) — each fixed-(n, D = 0), uniform in 1/B, Δ(1/B) from
Step 2. From each FFT: which tones are present, and which side is cleaner. A
clean spot check can be **decisive on its own**; lock its sampling, settling,
and sensitivity and hand them, with the measured onset, to Step 4.

**Step 4 — full Landau fan + per-column FFT (`landau-fan.md`).** Fan on the
cleaner side over a decently large density window at D = 0. Field range from
Step 3 (onset → B_lo; period-count extrapolation to the low-density edge sets
B_hi — the ABAB partner tone at the lowest fan density is the binding case).
Inherit the spot check's Δ(1/B) and settling. FFT each n-column; read peak set
vs F_L, the Luttinger partition, and each tone's n-dependence in one object.

**Step 5 — F(n) across density (the refinement).** (1) **Partition
robustness** — f₁(n) + f₂(n) = F_L(n) across density is algebraic (no model);
a coincidental one-density match will not hold. (2) **Branch labeling** —
overlay measured F(n) on the model curves (Verify: forward-model comparison):
ABAB branches are *both parabolic* and are labeled by the frequency ratio and
per-branch mass (Verify: LK), **not** by shape; a light *Dirac-shaped* branch
(supra-linear F(n) at low n against the model) points at ABCB's J = 1 partner
[citation-grade — report as candidate, hedge accordingly]. The binary
ABAB-pair vs ABCA-singleton call needs only (1) plus the F_L-tone origin
discrimination.

**Step 6 — high field (weak complement only).** There is **no tetralayer
Streda/Chern offset discriminator**: every 4L stacking carries 16 zero-energy
LLs — a ν = ±8, 12, 16 low-field ladder confirms the *layer number*, not the
stacking (survey §4; the layer-number check is itself useful — Verify:
adjacent-N). Stacking-dependent LL *fine structure* (two interleaved bilayer
ladders with mod-3 anticrossings vs a single bunched ladder) is qualitative —
no validated 4L LL model — so weight anything from it ≤ weak.

**Step 7 — the call.** Output contract (all five parts mandatory):

1. Per-region verdict on the STYLE strength scale: `channel/pair X: ABAB
   (strong) | ABCA (weak) | ABCB-candidate (consistent-with) | mixed-domain
   (consistent-with) | uninformative` — every verdict carries its weight word;
   bare leans are not verdicts.
2. Evidence list: each tone claimed, with frequency, (n, D) coordinates and
   density side, the Onsager-overlay artifact, and the Luttinger check.
3. Confidence + specific hedges (resolution limits, side/density, features
   searched-and-absent vs not-resolvable, domain/mosaic caveat, **absolute
   layer number** — if the peak set matches neither 4L template, the
   adjacent-N hypothesis belongs here before exotic explanations).
4. What would firm the call (other side, LK mass split, degeneracy audit,
   independent N-ID, a different rig/temperature).
5. **A "cannot tell" with reasons is a successful outcome. A confident call
   without feature-level evidence is a protocol violation.**

## Verify

- **TSV-first is mandatory for any classification-grade read.** Re-form
  Rxx(n, B) at native grid resolution (channel arithmetic per the device card)
  before any frequency claim; rendered monitor PNGs alias the SdH structure.
- **Onsager forward-model overlay.** Tool: `hera/models/tetralayer_fs_count/`
  (B = 0 FS count + Onsager F(n) + m*(n); ABAB SWMcC + ABCA 8-band continuum —
  semi-quantitative; validity stance in the model README). Overlay measured
  per-column F(n) allowing a **single global density rescale** (~0.8–1.2
  plausible [heuristic — lever-arm prior]; far outside that band is a red
  flag, not a fit) — fit that one scale to the **whole** peak set before
  reading any tone against a template; a lone tone forced onto a template by
  a private rescale while a resolved partner closes the Luttinger sum at
  scale 1 is a mis-read, not a fit. **A pair summing to F_L is necessary,
  not sufficient, for ABAB.** For any two-tone pair, compute **both**
  overlays — the ABAB curves *and* the trilayer ML+BL curves
  (`hera/models/trilayer_fs_count/`) — and report which family the branches
  track across density; **do not absorb a partition mismatch as model error**
  (the partition is a trusted model output — README validity stance): a pair
  tracking the trilayer curves is an adjacent-N read (Adjacent-N check
  below), not off-model ABAB [our-measurement, harness replay 2026-07-20 —
  agents mapped a trilayer 0.15/0.85 pair into 4L templates]. Partition
  magnitude alone cannot decide — the ABAB partner fraction sweeps
  ~0.06–0.44 with density and crosses the trilayer ~0.11–0.15 near
  |n| ≈ 2×10¹² [our-model]; the discriminator is the trajectory, not a
  ratio. Two branches on the ABAB curves *and* the F_L-tone origin passed is
  **strong** ABAB; a single branch on the ABCA curve with the origin
  discrimination passed is **strong** ABCA. Confound: mixed domains
  superpose templates on one F_L — resolve by the combinatorics, harmonic
  screen, and per-channel reads (Why).
- **F_L-tone origin (breakdown | ABCA domain | mixing) — mandatory before any
  singleton call where partner tones are resolved** (ABAB breakdown is
  symmetry-allowed, Why): (1) **B-window split** — FFT low-B and high-B halves
  separately; a breakdown/mixing tone strengthens with B relative to the
  fundamentals, a real pocket keeps its own Dingle envelope — but a *null*
  split in a narrow field window is weak: breakdown with onset scale above
  the window top is unresolvable there (absence claims cite resolvability)
  [our-model, synthetic replay]; (2) **grid-change
  reproduction** (`sdh-spot-check.md` Verify) retires sampling-alias origins;
  (3) the per-branch **LK mass** (below) is decisive. An unresolved remainder
  is a fork to report (STYLE rule 14).
- **LK mass split + beat exclusion** *(our-model expectation)*: the ABAB
  branches' masses differ by ≈ φ² ≈ 2.6× — per-branch LK masses
  (`temperature-dependence` Flavor B) cleanly separate two genuine bands from
  one band plus artifact; compare against the model's m*(n), never a
  light/heavy prior alone. Beat exclusion as in the trilayer sibling: a
  coexisting component **lighter** than the main branch cannot be a beat
  (decisive); at-or-above decides nothing alone.
- **Degeneracy audit.** F_L = (h/4e)·n assumes the symmetric 4-fold metal —
  expected at D ≈ 0, |n| ~ 10¹², kelvin-scale temperatures (survey §6), but
  verify in-data: after the scale is pinned on the full set, a peak set
  sitting at 2× or 4× its g = 4-predicted positions reads as flavor
  polarization (g = 2 / g = 1) and **suspends the g = 4 combinatorics** —
  escalate with the survey §6 reference rather than reading tones as
  supra-F_L pockets.
- **Adjacent-N check.** If the peak set matches neither 4L template **as a
  model overlay** — including a pair that sums to F_L but tracks the trilayer
  ML+BL curves rather than the ABAB curves (dual overlay above; a lopsided
  pair still passes the loose "pair partitioning F_L" template) — run the
  trilayer templates (ML+BL pair with a *small* partner; ABC singleton) and
  the pentalayer expectation (2+2+1) before anything exotic — optical-contrast
  N-assignment can misassign absolute layer number while resolving steps well
  (survey §7). Confound [our-model, synthetic replay]: a heavily damped
  singleton (large-m\* regions — e.g. the ABCA flat-band edge) plus a noise
  peak mimics the small-partner trilayer template on *single columns* — the
  adjacent-N call is a **cross-column consensus read**: the claimed partner
  must track its own Onsager curve across density and clear the local noise
  floor, never a one-column fit. A ν = 8, 12, 16 QH ladder (Step 6) or
  magneto-Raman G-band anticrossings (`hera/docs/papers/1501.06764/paper.md`)
  are independent N checks; state which N the transport actually supports in
  the hedges.
- **FFT stability sweep.** Vary detrender and window; a real peak sharpens as
  the 1/B record lengthens, an artifact wanders. Detrend on even-in-B data
  **before** interpolating to 1/B (detrending after manufactures
  low-frequency artifacts — paper-data, `hera/docs/papers/2606.05356/paper.md`
  resolution ladder). A frequency whose value or n-slope flips across
  reasonable extraction choices is a **fork to report, not refine** (STYLE
  rule 14).
- **Acquisition quality is empirical — compare at a shared density.** As in
  the trilayer sibling, verbatim: quality is a property of how a column was
  acquired; a lower-quality measurement never overturns a higher-quality one;
  the stopping rule (finer B resolves no new tones ⇒ count complete at this
  T/mobility) holds only on adequately acquired data. Resolution-ladder
  anchor: SdH from ≈ 0.1 T needs μ ≳ 10⁵ cm²/Vs (paper-data, Grushina — a
  suspended-device benchmark; expect a higher onset at lower quantum
  mobility, and read onset empirically in Step 3).
- **Luttinger sum.** Σf = n (g = 4) across the fan is the model-independent
  consistency check and the constraint that pins the global scale. A peak set
  that **cannot** satisfy the sum after the harmonic screen and stability
  sweep is a reportable state, not an extraction failure — R4G hosts
  documented non-Onsager regimes, though concentrated at large |D| / low n
  (survey §6); at the D ≈ 0 operating point treat it first as a degeneracy or
  N-assignment problem (audits above).
- **CNP magnitude is not a stacking read.** Insulating-CNP behavior has three
  candidate parents at N = 4 (survey §5) on top of the domain-shunting
  confound — feed it into the per-channel picture as consistent-with at
  most, never a standalone call.
- **Lever-arm / Nyquist at design time.** As in the trilayer sibling: ray
  slopes / frequencies must quantize against the (n, D) calibration; the
  B-axis SdH period sets the fan's B-row spacing — a fan failing the
  `landau-fan.md` Nyquist check in the claim window is uninformative there,
  re-measure.

## Examples

*(No live tetralayer sessions yet — this section seeds from the first
campaign/replay burns. Channel facts stay in device cards and notebook
indexes, never here — STYLE rule 11.)*

## Next

- **ABAB-confirmed** (pair partitioning F_L, Onsager-tracking, φ²-split LK
  masses): conventional tetralayer — campaign value is QH degeneracy-lifting /
  even-N interaction physics (ultraclean devices only); otherwise deprioritise.
- **ABCA-leaning** (singleton at F_L with the origin discrimination passed):
  the interesting outcome — flat-band / correlated / superconducting candidate
  at high D and mK temperatures (`hera/docs/papers/2606.05356/paper.md` for
  the phase-diagram map). Verify with D-gap systematics (per-channel,
  domain-aware) and plan the low-T campaign the physics deserves.
- **ABCB-candidate** (light Dirac partner + intrinsic-gap constellation):
  rare and citation-grade — what would firm it: Raman G-peak position and
  near-field imaging on the region, plus a model upgrade before any strong
  transport claim.
- **Mixed-domain device**: map which pairs probe which stacking; decide
  whether any single-domain region supports the science goal before more
  magnet time.
- **Resolution-limited cannot-tell**: state the onset-field / mobility number
  and what side, density, or temperature would change it — a device-quality /
  rig choice, not more sweeps on this rig.

2	
3	## What
4	A fixed-(n, D) magnetic-field sweep over a **low-field window**, designed to resolve
5	Shubnikov–de Haas / quantum-oscillation **frequency content** at one density — the
6	onset field and the tone frequencies — by FFT in 1/B. Mechanically this is a
7	`field-sweep-1d` (see it for the Station / sweep / fp / plot call surface); what
8	makes it a *spot check* is the design discipline below — the field range, 1/B spacing
9	Δ(1/B), and settling are chosen to resolve the tones cleanly, and the read is the 1/B
10	FFT.
11	It is the cheap 1D precursor to a `landau-fan`: one density, but **full per-point
12	quality**.
13	
14	## When
15	- **Before committing a `landau-fan`.** A spot check pins the **onset** (sets the
16	  fan's B-range), the **observed tone frequencies** (confirm/correct the fan's
17	  Δ(1/B)), and the **settling/sensitivity** the fan inherits. A fan is the dense
18	  version; a couple of clean spot checks de-risk it — and can answer the question
19	  outright (`investigations/trilayer-stacking-fs-count.md` Step 3).
20	- Whenever a `field-sweep-1d` or `gatemap` showed QO-like wiggles and you want the
21	  frequency content at a point, not the whole (n, B) plane.
22	
23	## Why
24	A spot check is cheap because it is **one density (1D), not because it is
25	low-quality**. Its whole value is being acquired *well* — at the settling floor and
26	Nyquist on the fastest tone — so a clean spot check can be decisive on its own and a
27	noisier fan cannot overturn it (`landau-fan`). Two knobs carry the quality:
28	
29	- **Sampling.** The fastest tone sets the finest 1/B period. The reference frequency
30	  **F_L = (h/g·e)·n** (g = 4) — what a single four-fold pocket carrying all the
31	  density would give — is an upper bound on the fastest tone; Nyquist it. Undersampling
32	  the fast tone folds its aliases into the low-frequency band, where they masquerade
33	  as a small/slow tone (Verify).
34	- **Settling.** A swept-point dwell has a floor near the lock-in time constant
35	  (dwell ≥ k·τ; k ≈ 5 at 6 dB/oct, 7–10 at 24 dB/oct). Under-settling **attenuates
36	  the oscillation amplitude itself** (the filter cannot track the QO) — benign on a
37	  smooth slope, but it *buries a small tone* (Verify). The floor is non-negotiable
38	  when the target is a weak tone.
39	
40	## Recipe
41	1. **Density + range.** Pick the density — high |n| gives the most periods and the
42	   clearest tones. Sweep a field window **[B_lo, B_hi]**; the sampling grid follows
43	   the magnet class:
44	   - **Field moves cheap** (non-blocking magnet): sample **uniformly in 1/B**
45	     (`field_invB`) — constant points-per-period, FFT the raw points (no resample).
46	     `B_lo` is a small positive floor (~0.1–0.3 T) below the expected **onset** (the
47	     lowest B where oscillations emerge once the MR background is subtracted) —
48	     uniform-1/B is densest in B at low field, so it captures the onset for free.
49	   - **Blocking rate-limited magnet** (traverse dominates wall-clock): sample
50	     **uniformly in B** with **ΔB = Δ(1/B)·B_lo²** (Nyquist held at the low-B edge;
51	     `sdh_fft` resamples internally). Same wall-clock — the points ride the traverse —
52	     with ≳30× the per-period averaging at high B and no blind ramps between sparse
53	     high-B points. ΔB scales as B_lo², so put `B_lo` just below the expected onset,
54	     not at a deep floor.
55	2. **Δ(1/B) from F_L.** Compute F_L = (h/4e)·n and Nyquist-resolve it: Δ(1/B) ≤ 1/(2·F_L)
56	   (prefer 1/3). Set N from the window: N = (1/B_lo − 1/B_hi)/Δ(1/B) + 1 uniform-1/B,
57	   N = (B_hi − B_lo)/ΔB + 1 uniform-B. This Δ(1/B) (and N) is what a committed fan
58	   inherits.
59	3. **δF from the record.** The tone resolution is set by the usable 1/B record above
60	   onset: **δF = 1/(1/B_onset − 1/B_max)** — tones closer than ~δF merge; trust a
61	   split only past ~2·δF. On high-T_e rigs the onset, not the field cap, sets δF:
62	   once 1/B_max ≪ 1/B_onset, raising B_max buys little — the lever is the
63	   density/side with the lower onset. Compute δF against the tones the claim must
64	   separate before sweeping.
65	4. **Lock-in.** Set sensitivity so full scale ≈ I_bias × R_target — a signal at a
66	   few % of range is coarse-ADC digitized (the grainy-FFT failure). Set the dwell at
67	   the settling floor (Why); read τ and the filter slope, do not guess them.
68	5. **The sweep.** Run it as a `field-sweep-1d` (its Recipe is the call surface):
69	   build the Station, ramp the gates to (n, D), `s.sweep(mag.field, B_vec,
70	   delay=dwell)` with the step-1 grid, fp the temperature(s) and every lock-in X/P,
71	   plot the live MR and gate-current leakage.
72	6. **FFT read.** Re-form Rxx from the TSV (rendered PNGs alias).
73	   - **Onset** — `hera.analysis.sdh_onset(R, B)` returns an `SdhOnset`: `onset_b` is
74	     the low-B edge of usable oscillation content (minimum over the tracked tones —
75	     a light tone that outlives the dominant one carries it), `clip_high_b` the high
76	     edge. `tones` holds each tone's own track: `freq`, per-tone `onset_b`,
77	     `snr`/`amp` curves over `b_centers`, `delta_f(b_max)` (that tone's usable-record
78	     resolution), and flags — `censored` (still above threshold at the record's low
79	     edge: `onset_b` is the record edge, not a measured die-off), `revived`,
80	     `marginal`, `near_residual`, and the bidirectional harmonic pair
81	     `harmonic_of` (this tone sits at k× a lower tone) / `harmonics` (freqs of
82	     tones sitting at k× of this one — a comb member is flagged from both ends
83	     regardless of which is stronger). Print `on.summary()` in the read
84	     cell. Pass `r_full_scale = sensitivity / I_bias` so a soft-clipped channel
85	     truncates the analysis window (with a warning) instead of feeding a flat-topped
86	     record to the FFT. Failure raises `SdhOnsetError` naming what was untrackable —
87	     that is a read result (no usable oscillations), not a prompt to eyeball.
88	   - **FFT** — `hera.analysis.sdh_fft(R_grid, B, *, b_range=(cutoff, B_max), bg_degree=5)`
89	     takes `R_grid` as `(n_B, n_fast)` — pass a single trace as `R[:, None]` — removes
90	     the MR background with a degree-`bg_degree` polynomial **in B** (the background is
91	     smooth in B, not 1/B), then FFTs in 1/B per column, and returns
92	     `(freqs, spec[n_fast, n_freq])` with `freqs` in Tesla. It needs a field range wide enough that
93	     the polynomial captures the background without absorbing the oscillations.
94	     `cutoff ≥ onset_b`, and often **above** it (Verify). Read the **tone frequencies**
95	     against F_L.
96	
97	## Verify
98	- **Settling — under-settling buries a small tone.** A dwell below the floor
99	  attenuates the oscillation amplitude (the filter can't track it). On a smooth slope
100	  that's a benign uniform lag; when the target is a small/weak tone it *erases* the
101	  feature. Non-negotiable for a weak-tone hunt; bend it only for a slope read on a
102	  strong signal.
103	- **Sampling — an undersampled fast tone aliases down.** If Δ(1/B) under-samples the
104	  fastest tone (≈ F_L), its aliases fold into the low-frequency band and masquerade
105	  as a small/slow tone. Nyquist the *fast* tone even when the target is the slow one
106	  (worked case: Examples).
107	- **Grid-change reproduction separates tones from aliases.** A real tone survives a
108	  change of sampling scheme (uniform-B vs uniform-1/B); an alias moves with the grid.
109	- **FFT stability sweep.** Vary `bg_degree` and the window; a real peak **sharpens**
110	  as the 1/B record lengthens, an alias/artifact **wanders**.
111	- **Onset is read from the background-subtracted data, not the FFT.** It is the
112	  low-field point where oscillations emerge in ΔRxx(B) (the MR background removed), not
113	  a quantity the FFT returns. It is a **lower bound** on the FFT low-field cutoff:
114	  residual background near the low-B end inflates the slowest tones, so raise the cutoff
115	  above the onset until the slow-tone amplitudes stop shrinking. Report the onset — it
116	  sets a fan's B-range and tracks quantum mobility (a rise on a later cooldown is a
117	  device-quality regression).
118	
119	## Examples
120	- *(our-measurement)* — a fine-step spot check resolved two tones (a main tone + a
121	  low-frequency partner), where a same-session fan run at a coarser B-step and
122	  under-settled did not. An earlier 4× coarser step had under-sampled the main tone,
123	  folding its aliases into the small-tone band. The worked case for "acquire the
124	  spot check well, *then* commit the fan."
125	
126	## Next
127	- **Clean QO, tones resolved** → run a `landau-fan`, inheriting this spot check's
128	  Δ(1/B), settling, and onset; or take a couple more spot checks across density for a
129	  cheap preview of the n-dependence.
130	- **Two tones at D ≈ 0** → `investigations/trilayer-stacking-fs-count.md` (the
131	  FS-count combinatorics).
132	- **Tone amplitude vs T wanted** (effective mass) → `temperature-dependence`
133	  Flavor B.

   separate before sweeping.
4. **Lock-in.** Set sensitivity so full scale ≈ I_bias × R_target — a signal at a
   few % of range is coarse-ADC digitized (the grainy-FFT failure). Set the dwell at
   the settling floor (Why); read τ and the filter slope, do not guess them.
5. **The sweep.** Run it as a `field-sweep-1d` (its Recipe is the call surface):
   build the Station, ramp the gates to (n, D), `s.sweep(mag.field, B_vec,
   delay=dwell)` with the step-1 grid, fp the temperature(s) and every lock-in X/P,
   plot the live MR and gate-current leakage.
6. **FFT read.** Re-form Rxx from the TSV (rendered PNGs alias).
   - **Onset** — `hera.analysis.sdh_onset(R, B)` returns an `SdhOnset`: `onset_b` is
     the low-B edge of usable oscillation content (minimum over the tracked tones —
     a light tone that outlives the dominant one carries it), `clip_high_b` the high
     edge. `tones` holds each tone's own track: `freq`, per-tone `onset_b`,
     `snr`/`amp` curves over `b_centers`, `delta_f(b_max)` (that tone's usable-record
     resolution), and flags — `censored` (still above threshold at the record's low
     edge: `onset_b` is the record edge, not a measured die-off), `revived`,
     `marginal`, `near_residual`, and the bidirectional harmonic pair
     `harmonic_of` (this tone sits at k× a lower tone) / `harmonics` (freqs of
     tones sitting at k× of this one — a comb member is flagged from both ends
     regardless of which is stronger). Print `on.summary()` in the read
     cell. Pass `r_full_scale = sensitivity / I_bias` so a soft-clipped channel
     truncates the analysis window (with a warning) instead of feeding a flat-topped
     record to the FFT. Failure raises `SdhOnsetError` naming what was untrackable —
     that is a read result (no usable oscillations), not a prompt to eyeball.
   - **FFT** — `hera.analysis.sdh_fft(R_grid, B, *, b_range=(cutoff, B_max), bg_degree=5)`
     takes `R_grid` as `(n_B, n_fast)` — pass a single trace as `R[:, None]` — removes
     the MR background with a degree-`bg_degree` polynomial **in B** (the background is
     smooth in B, not 1/B), then FFTs in 1/B per column, and returns
     `(freqs, spec[n_fast, n_freq])` with `freqs` in Tesla. It needs a field range wide enough that
     the polynomial captures the background without absorbing the oscillations.
     `cutoff ≥ onset_b`, and often **above** it (Verify). Read the **tone frequencies**
     against F_L.

## Verify
- **Settling — under-settling buries a small tone.** A dwell below the floor
  attenuates the oscillation amplitude (the filter can't track it). On a smooth slope
  that's a benign uniform lag; when the target is a small/weak tone it *erases* the
  feature. Non-negotiable for a weak-tone hunt; bend it only for a slope read on a
  strong signal.
- **Sampling — an undersampled fast tone aliases down.** If Δ(1/B) under-samples the
  fastest tone (≈ F_L), its aliases fold into the low-frequency band and masquerade
  as a small/slow tone. Nyquist the *fast* tone even when the target is the slow one
  (worked case: Examples).
- **Grid-change reproduction separates tones from aliases.** A real tone survives a
  change of sampling scheme (uniform-B vs uniform-1/B); an alias moves with the grid.
- **FFT stability sweep.** Vary `bg_degree` and the window; a real peak **sharpens**
  as the 1/B record lengthens, an alias/artifact **wanders**.
- **Onset is read from the background-subtracted data, not the FFT.** It is the
  low-field point where oscillations emerge in ΔRxx(B) (the MR background removed), not
  a quantity the FFT returns. It is a **lower bound** on the FFT low-field cutoff:
  residual background near the low-B end inflates the slowest tones, so raise the cutoff
  above the onset until the slow-tone amplitudes stop shrinking. Report the onset — it
  sets a fan's B-range and tracks quantum mobility (a rise on a later cooldown is a
  device-quality regression).

## Examples
- *(our-measurement)* — a fine-step spot check resolved two tones (a main tone + a
  low-frequency partner), where a same-session fan run at a coarser B-step and
  under-settled did not. An earlier 4× coarser step had under-sampled the main tone,
  folding its aliases into the small-tone band. The worked case for "acquire the
  spot check well, *then* commit the fan."

## Next
- **Clean QO, tones resolved** → run a `landau-fan`, inheriting this spot check's
  Δ(1/B), settling, and onset; or take a couple more spot checks across density for a
  cheap preview of the n-dependence.
- **Two tones at D ≈ 0** → `investigations/trilayer-stacking-fs-count.md` (the
  FS-count combinatorics).
- **Tone amplitude vs T wanted** (effective mass) → `temperature-dependence`
  Flavor B.

"""SdH spot-check read: runs 6 (electron n=+3.2e12) and 7 (hole n=-1.2e12).

import numpy as np, matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from hera.analysis import open_run, sdh_onset, sdh_fft, luttinger_frequency, resolve_channels

BASE = "/home/hera/measurements/zack/20260822-vti-02/data"

def read(rid, n_cm2, label):
    run = open_run(f"{BASE}/{rid}")
    B = run.col("magnet_field")
    ch = resolve_channels(run)
    print(f"-- run {rid} channels:", {k: (v.role if hasattr(v,'role') else v) for k,v in ch.items()} if isinstance(ch, dict) else ch)
    # sr1 = Rxx (B_1-B_2), gain 1; I_bias from metadata
    mc = run.meta["measurement_config"]
    ibias = None
    # I_bias: sr1 drive amplitude / bias resistor -- take from instruments snapshot if present
    sens = None
    inst = run.meta.get("instruments", {})
    sr1 = inst.get("sr1", {})
    amp = sr1.get("amplitude"); sens = sr1.get("sensitivity")
    Rbias = mc["bias_resistor"]
    if amp: ibias = amp / Rbias
    print(f"   sr1 amplitude={amp}, sensitivity={sens}, I_bias={ibias}")
    R = run.col("sr1_X") / ibias
    FL = luttinger_frequency(n_cm2)

    try:

        on, onset = None, None
    return run, B, R, FL, on, onset

content.content:
# Tetralayer FS-count forward model — ABAB vs ABCA (vs ABCB)

Backs the `recipes/investigations/tetralayer-stacking-fs-count.md` investigation.
This model computes the **B = 0 Fermi-surface count**, the **Onsager
frequencies F(n)** (and vs interlayer potential u_D for ABCA), and the
**cyclotron masses m\*(n)** the FS-count read overlays on data — ABAB a pair
partitioning F_L (≈ 0.72 / 0.28 with φ²-split masses in the decomposition
limit; the key table below carries the real F(n)) vs ABCA's single
post-cascade pocket at F_L, with ABCB a qualitative cubic + Dirac pair.
**Both carrier signs**: the sign of the input density selects electron
(n > 0) or hole (n < 0) doping.

The survey that grounds it (band structure, the four ingested papers, the
feasibility framing) is `docs/tetralayer-stacking-extraction-survey.md`; read
it for the physics. This README covers what the tools are and how to run them.

## Files

| File | What it does |
|---|---|
| `synth_fan.py` | Synthetic Rxx(n, B) fan generator on the model's F(n)/m\*(n): LK thermal + Dingle dressing, 2nd harmonics, background, noise; optional lever-arm scale error, breakdown sum-tone, mixed-domain superposition. Ground truth per column in `truth.json`. |
| `synth_eval.py` | Mechanical recipe evaluator over the synthetic fans (pipeline FFT → Luttinger-aware harmonic screen → global scale pin → template match → B-window split → adjacent-N). Six-case suite + `RESULTS.md` in `$HERA_DATA/tetralayer-synth-validation/`. |
| `JULIA_CROSSCHECK.md` | Independent-implementation eigenvalue comparison (machine precision; see Validation). |

## HERA — SdH onset extension, electron side (`sdh-spot-check`), before the fan

Spot-check read (runs 6/7, ana to follow): electron side is the cleaner side — dominant tone **7.1 T** (SNR 40–90) with a 2×/3×/4× comb (14.1/22.1/29.5 T) against F_L = 33.1 T; model ABAB at n = +3.2e12 predicts 7.31 (light) + 25.78 T (heavy), so the observed 22.1 T tone is either the ABAB heavy pocket or the 3× harmonic of 7.1 — the recipe's warned confound, resolved by n-trajectories in the fan, not by δF here. Hole side (run 7) is the predicted near-CNP exception regime (close, balanced tones) — the fan goes electron.

**Why this cell first**: run 6's carrying tone is `censored` at the record's low edge — its 50 mT low-B leg undersamples 7.1 T below ~0.84 T, so the onset (which sets the fan's B_lo, the most expensive design lever) is unmeasured; `landau-fan.md` step 1 prescribes a cheap low-field extension before committing the fan. Hole-side measured onset is 0.71 T; LK at T_e ≈ 8 K, m* ≈ 0.027 says the light tone should die between ~0.7 and 1 T. This 5 mT leg (3× Nyquist on 7.1 T down to 0.33 T) measures it; the fan's B_lo = the measured onset (each 0.1 T of B_lo saved/spent moves the fan by roughly ±1 h). Overlap 1.0–1.32 T with run 6's 10 mT leg doubles as the grid-change reproduction check (Verify).

Preconditions on the page: T ≈ 1.2 K, B = 0 (handoff state), V_si = 0, PS heater/output on. Gates ramp to the run-6 spot and stay; field ends at 1.32 T, from which the fan positions.
